issues.description: Method parameter inconsistency for messageOnMilk: The problem statement (Part 2) describes a Milkable method messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) that accepts a double parameter and expects the returned string to include the volume. However, the UML in the problem statement, the template usage in Main.java, and the solution code define messageOnMilk() as a no-argument method (signature: String messageOnMilk()) and implementations (Seal, Goat) return strings without any volume information. This contradictory specification of the same method will cause students to implement the wrong signature (leading to compilation/test failures) or be uncertain which API to follow.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the method signature and examples consistent across all artifacts. Recommended actions:
1) If tests and template expect no-argument messageOnMilk(), update problem_statement.md (Part 2) to describe messageOnMilk() with no parameters and show the example return value without volume (e.g. "[Animal Type] [name] is milked").
OR
2) If the volume parameter is pedagogically required, update the template, solution, and all call sites (e.g., Main.java and any tests) to declare String messageOnMilk(double milkVolume), update Seal/Goat implementations to accept the double parameter and include the volume in the returned string (e.g. "Seal Clarabelle is milked (volume: 1.5L)"), and update any callers accordingly.
Apply exactly one of these two consistent choices across problem text, template, and solution to avoid compilation errors and student confusion.
